issues.title: Compactness of sublevel sets (A2) fails for the NMF/CP objectives on the nonnegative orthant
issues.why_classification: The compact-constraint resolution is a limited weakening that leaves recognizably comparable complexity results; a full resolution for the orthant constraints requires a new nontrivial argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The function $g_{n}^{(i)}$ in \eqref{eq:BProxLinear} is indeed a majorizing surrogate of $f_{n}^{(i)}$ when the objective $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $\lambda \ge L$.

for each compact subset $\Param_{0}\subseteq \Param$, there exist a constant $L_{f}=L_{f}(\Param_{0})$ such that $\lVert \nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y) \rVert\le L_{f} \lVert x-y \rVert$ for all $x,y\in \Param_{0}$.
\item{(1)} (Majorization) $g_{n}^{(i)}(\theta)- f_{n}^{(i)}(\theta) \ge 0$ for all $\theta \in \Theta^{(i)}$;

Suppose \ref{assumption:A1} and \ref{assumption:A2} hold, where the convex constraint sets $\Theta^{(i)}$ are not necessarily bounded. Further, assume that the stepsize $1/\lambda$ is sufficiently small.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption A2 provides Lipschitz continuity of grad f only on compact subsets, while the framework requires majorization g_n^{(i)} >= f_n^{(i)} (condition (1)) and the quadratic gap eq:majorization_gap_lower_bd for all theta in Theta^{(i)}, and Assumption A5(b) requires globally Lipschitz surrogate gradients. For prox-linear surrogates these can all fail when grad f is only locally Lipschitz: f(x) = x^4 on Theta = R satisfies A1-A2, but for any lambda, g(x) - f(x) = f(x_0) + f'(x_0)(x - x_0) + (lambda/2)(x - x_0)^2 - x^4 -> -infinity as |x| -> infinity, so no stepsize makes eq:BProxLinear a majorizing surrogate on all of Theta^{(i)}. All proofs use these conditions only on the compact set Param_0 of Proposition prop:boundedness.

failure_location.quote: In the introduction, we discussed that the block projected gradient descent (BPGD) \eqref{eq:BPGD} is a special instance of BMM where prox-linear surrogates are exactly minimized over convex constraint sets.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add global L-smoothness of f (with lambda > L) to the corollary's hypotheses, or restate condition (1), eq:majorization_gap_lower_bd and eq:surrogate_L_smoothness locally on Param_0; the proofs already use them only there, so all conclusions are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:BPGD -- the claimed first O~(eps^{-2}) complexity for block PGD -- is not covered by Theorem thm:complexity as stated for objectives that are only locally smooth, a regime Assumption A2 allows and the corollary does not exclude.
issues.title: Block PGD under merely locally Lipschitz gradients does not satisfy the framework's global surrogate conditions
issues.why_classification: A one-line additional hypothesis (or local restatement of the conditions) repairs the reduction with no loss of method, rate, or advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (ALS with DR)  \quad $g_{n}^{(i)}=f_{n}^{(i)}$, $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} r_{n}=\infty, \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} r_{n}^{2}<\infty$.
BMM-DR \eqref{eq:ALS_DR_PR_CTF} is implemented on top of BMM with diminishing radius with parameter $\beta=0.1$ and same $c'$ as BCD-DR.
Similarly, a proper value of $\beta$ is also crucial for fast convergence, here as shown in Figure \ref{fig:benchmark}, BCD-DR with $\beta=0.1$ attains its best performance.

issues.failure_explanation: The caption and text state that BCD-DR and BMM-DR are implemented as the analyzed options eq:ALS_DR_CTF/eq:ALS_DR_PR_CTF, which require sum r_n^2 < infinity, but the experiments use r_n = n^{-beta}/log n with beta = 0.1, for which sum n^{-0.2}/(log n)^2 = infinity. The numerical results for the paper's namesake diminishing-radius methods are therefore obtained outside the regime covered by Theorem thm:complexity, and beta = 0.1 is advertised as the best-performing choice, so these experiments neither illustrate nor support the proven guarantees (which need beta > 1/2).

failure_location.quote: BCD-DR is implemented as \eqref{eq:BMM_DR_CTF}\eqref{eq:ALS_DR_CTF} with $c'=\lVert \mathbf{X} \rVert_{F}/(1.5\times 10^{5})$ for synthetic data and $c'=\lVert \mathbf{X} \rVert_{F}/(3\times 10^{5})$ for Cifar10 data  ($\mathbf{X}$ denoting the data tensor) and weights $r_{n}=n^{-\beta}/\log n$ for $n\ge 1$ for both.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use beta > 1/2 (e.g., the theoretically motivated r_n = 1/(sqrt(n) log n)) or state explicitly that the experiments operate outside the proven regime.
issues.overall_effect: The experimental validation of BCD-DR/BMM-DR does not correspond to the analyzed algorithms; no formal result is affected, but the claimed validation of the diminishing-radius contribution is misleading.
issues.title: Experiments run the diminishing-radius algorithms outside the analyzed square-summable regime
issues.why_classification: Only the experimental setup and prose are concerned; formal results are unaffected; a parameter change or disclosure suffices.
